Police Report: At about 5:24 PM, a clerk at a small retail store in the 036XX block of E 106th St reported that a customer's card was declined at the register. The customer stepped back from the counter, moved to an aisle, and placed phone chargers and cosmetics in a tote bag. The clerk called out and stood near the door. The customer said "I already paid" and walked around the clerk without touching or threatening them, leaving on foot with the unpaid items. The clerk was not hurt. Surveillance footage will be reviewed. No arrest was made.

Officers responded to a residence in the 056XX block of S Laflin St at about 2:30 PM for a domestic disturbance. The victim stated that during an argument about rent, a family member threw a dinner plate against the wall, stepped in close with a raised fist, and said "you're next." The victim backed into the hallway, believing they were about to be hit. The family member never touched the victim, and the plate was the only item broken. No injuries were observed. The family member had left before officers arrived, and no arrest was made.

The victim reported that at about 12:00 PM they went to an apartment in the 061XX block of S Kimbark Ave to collect $200 an acquaintance owed them. During an argument at the door, the acquaintance lifted a handgun from their waistband, pointed it at the victim, and told them to leave and forget about the money. The victim left immediately. No shots were fired, there was no physical contact, and nothing was taken from the victim. Officers found no shell casings. The acquaintance was gone when officers arrived, no weapon was recovered, and no arrest was made.

The victim parked on the street in the 012XX block of N California Ave and returned at about 11:00 PM to find the passenger door ajar and the glove box open. A work bag holding a tablet was missing from the floor of the vehicle. The victim was not sure whether they had locked the doors. The windows and locks were intact, and the vehicle itself was still in place and started normally. Officers canvassed the block but found no witnesses or cameras. No offender was identified and no arrest was made.

The victim reported that at about 9:50 AM they were on a crowded CTA train at the Roosevelt station, in the 0000X block of E Roosevelt Rd, when a person standing next to them bumped them as the doors opened and then got off. Minutes later the victim found the side pocket of their backpack unzipped and a tablet and headphones, valued at about $900, gone. The victim was not sure the bump was intentional. They did not feel anything pulled from them, were not threatened, and were not hurt. CTA will be asked for video. No arrest was made.

At about 7:00 PM, officers on patrol saw a subject striking a city-owned parking pay station with a metal pipe in a non-residential parking lot in the 0000X block of W 111th St. The screen was shattered and the coin door was dented, but the door remained closed and no money was removed. The subject appeared upset and told officers the machine had taken their money without printing a receipt. The subject dropped the pipe when ordered and made no threats toward officers. The subject was taken into custody, and the city department responsible for the machine was notified.

Officers responded to an apartment in the 132XX block of S St Lawrence Ave at about 5:00 AM for a domestic disturbance. The victim stated that their partner came home and started an argument over text messages, then pushed the victim against a wall and slapped them across the face. The partner also grabbed the victim's phone and tossed it onto the couch, where officers found it undamaged. Slight swelling was visible on the victim's cheek, and the victim declined medical attention. The partner left before officers arrived. Domestic violence resources were provided and no arrest was made.

Description: AGGRAVATED DOMESTIC BATTERY - KNIFE / CUTTING INSTRUMENT
Police Report: Officers responded to an apartment in the 007XX block of S California Ave at about 6:00 AM. The victim stated that a household member picked up a kitchen knife during an argument, yelled that the victim would regret leaving, and then slashed at them, cutting their forearm as they raised it to protect themselves. Paramedics treated the laceration at the scene and the injury was not life-threatening. A lamp was also knocked over during the struggle. The knife was recovered and inventoried. The household member fled before officers arrived, was not located, and no arrest was made.

At about 10:40 AM, a customer at a grocery store in the 025XX block of N Central Ave reported that their wallet, holding about $80 in cash, was taken from their shopping cart. The customer stated that a stranger asked them for help reading a label in the next aisle, and that the wallet was gone when they returned to the cart moments later. The customer was never touched or threatened. Their bank cards were canceled, and no charges had been made on them. The store will review its footage. No offender was identified and no arrest was made.

At about 3:22 AM, officers responded to a report of noise in the 016XX block of N California Ave and found the access panel of a city-owned street light pried from its base, with pry marks around the opening. Wiring inside was cut and pulled loose, but none of it had been removed, and the light was out. Tools were not found at the scene. A resident heard metal scraping but did not see anyone. There was no sign that a vehicle had struck the pole. The city was notified for repair. No offender was identified and no arrest was made.

The victim reported that at about 5:35 PM they found the rear side window of their vehicle broken while it was parked on the street in the 025XX block of W Fitch Ave. A long scratch ran along the driver's door. A bag of groceries and loose change in the cupholder were still in plain view and appeared undisturbed, and nothing was missing. The victim mentioned an earlier dispute with a neighbor over the parking space, but no one saw who did this. A neighbor heard glass breaking but saw no one. No arrest was made.

Officers responded to an apartment in the 038XX block of N St Louis Ave at about 2:33 PM. The victim stated that their spouse blocked the bedroom doorway during an argument over money, then grabbed their arm and shoved them onto the bed. The spouse said they would take the car keys if the victim tried to leave, but the keys stayed with the victim and the victim was able to leave the room. Redness was visible on the victim's arm, and the victim declined medical attention. The spouse had left before officers arrived. Domestic violence resources were provided and no arrest was made.

The victim reported that at about 3:20 PM they set their phone, valued at about $300, on a ledge while tying a shoe on the sidewalk in the 025XX block of W 39th Pl. A person on foot picked it up and started walking quickly away. The victim shouted and followed for half a block, but the person began to run and was lost from view near an alley. The two never came within arm's reach of each other, and the person did not speak to the victim or display anything. The victim was not hurt. No arrest was made.

At about 6:23 PM, officers on patrol in the 105XX block of S Avenue N saw a subject on the street put something in their mouth, then spit it out as officers approached. The item was a small plastic bag containing a white powder, which field-tested positive for cocaine. A folding pocketknife and $40 in cash were also in the subject's possession. Officers saw no exchange with anyone else and found no scales or packaging materials. The subject complied with officers during the stop. The subject was taken into custody, and the items were inventoried.

Description: AGG. DOMESTIC BATTERY - HANDS, FISTS, FEET, SERIOUS INJURY
Police Report: Officers responded to an apartment in the 070XX block of S Indiana Ave at about 12:09 PM. The victim stated that a household member accused them of taking money, then punched them in the face and kicked them repeatedly after they fell. No weapon was used. The victim was found with a swollen eye and difficulty breathing and was taken to a hospital, where they were treated for a broken nose and fractured ribs. A coffee table was broken in the struggle. The household member fled before officers arrived. The case was referred to detectives and no arrest has been made.

At about 11:24 PM, officers on patrol saw a subject in an alley in the 055XX block of W North Ave drop a handgun behind a garbage cart as the squad car approached. A faint smell of cannabis was noted on the subject, but none was found. The subject did not point the gun at anyone, and no one reported being threatened. The subject first said they had a concealed carry permit, but a records check showed they had never been issued a firearm owner's card or a carry license. The loaded handgun was inventoried, and the subject was taken into custody.

At about 3:51 PM, the victim reported that a generator and power tools valued at about $1,400 were gone from the back porch of their residence in the 021XX block of W 72nd Pl. The porch is open to the yard and has no door. The house itself was locked, none of its doors or windows were touched, and nothing inside was disturbed. A neighbor recalled a pickup truck in the alley earlier that day but could not describe the driver. No arrest was made.

At about 3:20 PM, a student at a college building in the 0000X block of E Jackson Blvd reported that their laptop bag was gone after they left it on a study table to use the restroom. The building was open to the public at the time and no doors or lockers were forced. A staff member remembered someone walking out with a similar bag but could not give a description. No one confronted the student. Campus security will review its cameras. No arrest was made.

At about 7:10 PM, officers stopped a vehicle in the 008XX block of W 119th St because its paper temporary plate looked handwritten. The expiration date had been changed with a marker, and the number came back to a different vehicle. A check of the VIN showed that the car belonged to the driver and had not been reported missing. The driver said a friend had given them the plate after the old one expired. The driver was taken into custody, and the plate was inventoried.

Officers responded to an apartment in the 047XX block of S Michigan Ave at about 8:20 AM. The victim stated that their girlfriend came into the kitchen yelling about a phone bill and grabbed them by the shirt, scratching their neck. The girlfriend also threatened to throw out the victim's clothes but did not do so. A small scratch was visible and the victim declined medical attention. The girlfriend left for work before officers arrived. Domestic violence resources were provided and no arrest was made.

The victim reported that at about 2:00 AM they heard a loud bang from the street in the 014XX block of W Potomac Ave and came outside to find their parked vehicle's rear window shattered. A brick lay on the back seat. A laptop bag left on the front seat was still there, the glove box was closed, and nothing was missing. No doors had been opened. Two people were heard running toward an alley but were not seen clearly. No arrest was made.

At about 8:45 AM, a manager at a restaurant in the 051XX block of W Chicago Ave reported that the front window had been cracked and a patio table overturned and broken. Staff said a customer who had been refused a refund the previous evening had threatened to come back. Cash in the register and all equipment were accounted for, and the door lock was untouched, with no sign anyone had gone inside. Security video was unclear. No arrest was made.

At about 12:00 PM, the victim reported that a watch and a gold chain worth about $1,100 were gone from a dresser in their apartment in the 014XX block of W Roosevelt Rd. The victim had let a temporary roommate stay for two weeks, and the roommate moved out the day before with a key the victim gave them. There was no sign of forced entry and the door was not damaged. The roommate has stopped answering calls. No arrest was made.

At about 9:00 AM, the victim called officers to their residence in the 057XX block of N Kingsdale Ave and showed them a court order barring their former husband from the home. The victim stated that the former husband had come onto the porch, left a note, and rung the bell repeatedly. He did not threaten or touch the victim and did not try to force the door. The note was collected, and the order was confirmed as active and served. He left before officers arrived, and no arrest was made.

At about 3:00 PM, the victim returned to their car, parked on the street in the 091XX block of S Colfax Ave, and found all four tires slashed and a key scratch along the hood. The car's doors were still locked, and the personal items left inside were undisturbed. The victim said a former coworker had been sending angry messages, but no one saw who was responsible. A neighbor's camera did not cover that part of the street. No arrest was made.

The victim reported that they parked their car on the street in the 011XX block of N State St and returned at about 5:00 PM to find it gone. Broken glass from a side window was on the pavement where it had been parked. The victim had both sets of keys. A check with the city confirmed the car had not been towed or impounded. No one has permission to use it, and the victim's payments are current. The car's plate was entered into the system. No arrest was made.

At about 1:17 AM, officers responded to the 117XX block of S Normal Ave after a resident reported hearing glass breaking. The resident's parked vehicle had a smashed windshield and a dented hood. A baseball bat lay in the grass nearby. Nobody was in the vehicle at the time, and the resident was never approached or threatened. A stereo and sunglasses inside were not touched. The resident said they had argued with an unknown driver over a parking spot that afternoon. No arrest was made.

At about 3:13 PM, loss prevention staff at a drug store in the 004XX block of N Michigan Ave reported that a shopper filled a bag with skin care products and walked past the registers. When a staff member approached outside and asked to see a receipt, the shopper said they would come back with it and kept walking. There was no physical contact and no weapon was seen. The shopper boarded a bus before officers arrived. Footage was saved, and no arrest was made.

At about 9:00 AM, the victim reported that a leaf blower and a toolbox, worth about $250 together, were taken from the open bed of their pickup while it was parked on the street in the 066XX block of S Marquette Rd. The truck's cab stayed locked, and its windows and doors were not damaged. The victim was working in a nearby yard and did not see anyone. A neighbor saw a person walking off with a toolbox but thought they were a worker. No arrest was made.

The victim reported at about 6:00 PM that they had left their car running to warm up on the street in the 020XX block of W Armitage Ave while they ran into a shop. When they came back two minutes later, it was gone. The victim had not given anyone permission to drive it. No one was hurt or confronted, since the victim was inside the shop. The vehicle was not found during a check of the surrounding blocks, and its plate was entered into the system. No arrest was made.

Officers responded to an apartment in the 013XX block of S Washtenaw Ave at about 9:54 PM. The victim stated that their brother became angry over a borrowed car, picked up a chair, and held it above his head while yelling that he would crush them. The victim ran to the bathroom and locked the door. The brother put the chair down and did not strike the victim or the door. No injuries were observed. He left before officers arrived, and no arrest was made.

At about 9:52 PM, the victim reported that their boyfriend had moved out of their shared apartment in the 009XX block of W 95th St that evening and taken the victim's game console, TV, and jewelry, valued at about $1,300. The boyfriend had a key and lived there, so nothing was forced. There was no argument or physical confrontation, as the victim was at work. He has blocked the victim's number. The victim provided receipts for the items. No arrest was made.

At about 2:54 PM, officers stopped a car in the 071XX block of S Marshfield Ave for a paper temporary plate that appeared to have been printed at home. A database check showed that the plate number had never been issued. The car's VIN showed that the driver had bought it legally from a private seller. The driver said they had paid someone online for the plate and did not know it was not valid. The driver was taken into custody, and the plate was inventoried as evidence.

At about 8:00 PM, a customer at a restaurant in the 012XX block of N Clybourn Ave reported that another diner shoved them in the chest after an argument over a spilled drink. The victim fell back into a chair but was not seriously hurt. Several plates fell and broke in the commotion, and the owner did not wish to pursue the cost. The other diner paid the bill and left before officers arrived. Staff could not identify them. No arrest was made.

Description: GUN OFFENDER - DUTY TO REPORT CHANGE OF INFORMATION
Police Report: At about 9:19 PM, officers stopped a pedestrian on the street in the 042XX block of W Fullerton Ave to ask about a nearby disturbance. A records check showed the subject was on the gun offender registry and had moved two months earlier without updating their address with the police. The subject said they had meant to report the move. A pat-down found no firearm or contraband, and the subject was not connected to the disturbance. The subject was taken into custody for failing to report the change.

At about 10:17 PM, a shift manager at a restaurant in the 045XX block of N Kedzie Ave reported that a person walked in, took two packs of bottled drinks and a box of snacks from a self-service display, and left without paying. The person had not ordered a meal. An employee called after them from the doorway, but no one followed. No threats were made and nobody was hurt. The person left in a dark sedan, and no arrest was made.

At about 5:35 AM, the victim was walking on the street in the 0000X block of E Superior St when two people stepped out from behind a parked van. One pointed a handgun at the victim and demanded their phone and wallet. The victim handed them over, and the pair ran to a waiting car. No shots were fired and the victim was not touched or injured. Officers searched the area and found neither the offenders nor the property. A nearby business will provide video. No arrest was made.

At about 10:30 PM, the victim reported that their SUV was gone from the spot where they parked it on the street in the 044XX block of N Kenton Ave. The victim's spouse confirmed they had not moved it. The victim could not find their spare key and thought it might have been left in the center console. No tow record exists for the vehicle. There was no broken glass at the location. The plate was entered into the system, and no arrest was made.

At about 3:30 PM, a building owner in the 050XX block of W 47th St reported that the door frame of a vacant apartment had been kicked and split and that the walls of the hallway had been spray-painted. The owner said the door held and did not open. Tenants reported hearing shouting earlier, but no one saw who did it. Nothing inside the unit was touched. The owner provided photographs and a repair estimate. No arrest was made.

At about 6:00 AM, the victim, who lives in an apartment in the 081XX block of S Ingleside Ave, reported that their ex-boyfriend had called repeatedly overnight from a blocked number. In one voicemail he said he would burn the place down with the victim inside. No one came to the apartment, and nothing has happened to the property. There is no court order in place. The victim saved the voicemail for officers. The ex-boyfriend has not been located, and no arrest was made.

At about 5:40 PM, the victim reported that they had set a motorized scooter valued at about $700 down on the street in the 040XX block of W Madison St while they helped a friend unload a car. When they turned around, a person was riding it away. The scooter was unlocked. The victim yelled but did not chase the rider. Nobody spoke to the victim, and no force or threat was used. Officers checked the area but did not find the scooter. No arrest was made.

At about 2:05 AM, a resident in the 030XX block of W 61st St saw two people get into their sedan, parked on the street, and drive it away. The resident ran outside but was too far away to speak to them, and no threats or weapons were involved. The keys were still in the resident's pocket, and pieces of a plastic steering column cover were found at the curb. The car has not been found. Its plate was entered into the system, and no arrest was made.

At about 5:00 AM, the victim, a delivery driver, reported that a package cart worth about $300, with its load, had been taken from the street in the 070XX block of S Jeffery Blvd while they were making a delivery. The van was not entered. Nobody spoke to the driver. A person pushing a similar cart was later seen a few blocks away, but the cart could not be found. The package contents are being checked with the company. No arrest was made.

At about 1:48 PM, loss prevention at a department store in the 011XX block of W Jackson Blvd saw a shopper remove tags from a jacket in a fitting room, put it on under a coat, and walk out past the registers. Staff stopped the shopper on the sidewalk. The shopper claimed the jacket had been bought last week and pulled their arm back when staff approached, but no one was struck. Officers arrived and the shopper was taken into custody. The jacket was recovered.

At about 1:00 AM, an alarm brought officers to a restaurant in the 061XX block of S Archer Ave. The rear door had been pried open and the frame splintered. The cash drawer was on the floor, and about $350 was gone from it. No employees were present when it happened, and no one was confronted. Liquor bottles and kitchen equipment were left in place. Video showed a hooded figure inside for about four minutes. The owner secured the door. No arrest was made.

Officers responded to a residence in the 087XX block of S Marquette Ave at about 1:40 AM for a domestic disturbance. The victim stated that their husband came home intoxicated and pushed them to the floor during an argument, leaving a scrape on one elbow. A framed photo fell and broke. The husband admitted that they had argued but said the victim had tripped. Officers observed the scrape and the victim declined treatment. The husband was taken into custody.

The victim reported at about 1:00 PM that they had parked in a non-residential garage in the 0000X block of E 9th St and left a rear door unlocked. When they returned, a suitcase and a pair of headphones were gone from the back seat. The vehicle was still in its parking space and showed no signs of damage, and the windows were intact. The garage attendant saw nothing unusual. Video from the garage will be requested. No arrest was made.

At about 11:40 PM, the victim reported that they had leaned their $800 bicycle against a pole on the street in the 006XX block of E 62nd St to answer a phone call a few feet away. A passerby got on the bike and rode off. The victim called out, but the rider did not stop. No one touched or threatened the victim. The bike was not locked. Officers searched nearby streets but did not find it. No arrest was made.

Officers responded to an apartment in the 064XX block of S Greenwood Ave at about 8:40 PM. The victim stated that their sister-in-law, angry over a child care disagreement, threw a shoe that missed them and hit the wall, then rushed toward them with her hand raised. The victim stepped back and closed a door. No one was touched and nothing was broken. The sister-in-law left when the victim said they were calling police. No injuries were reported and no arrest was made.

At about 9:00 AM, the victim returned to their apartment in the 021XX block of W Wellington Ave after a night away and found the back door kicked in and the frame broken. A laptop, camera, and jewelry were gone, and drawers had been emptied onto the floor. No one was home when it happened. The victim knew of no one who had a key. Neighbors had not heard anything. An evidence technician processed the scene for fingerprints. No arrest was made.

At about 11:11 PM, officers responded to the sidewalk in the 010XX block of W Lawrence Ave after a caller reported a person pulling down a business's sidewalk sign and throwing a newspaper box. The sign frame was bent and its glass was shattered. No one was struck, and no one claimed to have been threatened. The items had not been removed from the block. The owner of the sign said it would need replacing. The person walked off before officers arrived, and no arrest was made.

Description: SEX OFFENDER - FAIL TO REGISTER NEW ADDRESS
Police Report: At about 3:55 AM, officers stopped a pedestrian on the street in the 032XX block of W 26th St during a routine check of the area. A records search showed the subject was on the state sex offender registry and had not reported a new address after moving a month earlier. There was no complaint from anyone about the subject that night, and the subject had no contraband. The subject said they were between homes. The subject was taken into custody for failing to register.

Officers responded to an apartment in the 028XX block of S Komensky Ave at about 9:30 PM during Fourth of July fireworks. The victim stated that their boyfriend became jealous at a family gathering, then grabbed them by the hair and slapped them in the bedroom. Officers saw redness on the victim's face. The boyfriend said it was only an argument, but a relative confirmed seeing the slap. No weapons were involved. The victim declined treatment. The boyfriend was taken into custody.

At about 2:00 PM, the victim reported that their ex-girlfriend pulled up alongside them on the street in the 080XX block of S Cottage Grove Ave, got out, and stepped toward them with a raised tire iron, yelling that she was going to "bust them up." The victim backed into a store. The tire iron was not swung, and she did not touch the victim or the victim's car. She got back in her vehicle and drove off. No injuries were reported and no arrest was made.

At about 8:45 AM, a security officer on public school grounds in the 011XX block of W 66th St reported that a parent, upset about a bus incident, stepped up close to a teacher near the entrance, pointed in the teacher's face, and said "I'll knock you out." The teacher stepped back and went inside, fearing they would be struck. No contact was made, and the parent never entered the building. The parent drove away before officers arrived. No injuries were reported and no arrest was made.

At about 9:00 AM, a homeowner in the 014XX block of S Hamlin Ave reported that their wooden fence had been knocked down and a mailbox torn off its post overnight. Footprints in the snow led to the alley. The homeowner did not know of any dispute with neighbors. Nothing was taken from the yard, and the house and garage were secure. A neighbor's tools stored near the fence were left where they were. No witnesses were found, and no arrest was made.

At about 3:25 PM, the victim returned to their apartment in the 081XX block of S Loomis Blvd to find the door frame splintered and a TV gone. A neighbor saw the victim's ex-husband leaving with the TV and a box. He moved out months earlier, is not on the lease, and has no key. No one was home, so there was no confrontation. The victim had the lock replaced. The ex-husband could not be located, and no arrest was made.

At about 9:00 PM, the victim found that all the windows on the passenger side of their car, parked on the street in the 106XX block of S Sangamon St, had been broken. A bucket of tools on the back seat and a phone charger were still in the car. The victim said that nothing was missing after going through the vehicle with officers. A dog walker heard a loud noise but did not see anyone. No arrest was made.

At about 6:50 PM, the owner of a small retail store in the 052XX block of W Madison St stopped a customer at the door after seeing them put phone cases and razors in their jacket. The customer pulled the items out, set them on the counter, and said they had forgotten to pay. Officers reviewed video showing the items being hidden. No force was used by anyone, and no weapon was seen. The owner signed a complaint, and the customer was taken into custody.

At about 4:55 PM, the victim reported that during an argument over a double-parked car on the street in the 008XX block of N St Louis Ave, the other driver lifted a shirt to show a handgun, then took it out and pointed it at them, saying "move it or else." The victim moved the car and drove to a safe location. No shots were fired, nothing was demanded other than moving the car, and no one was hit. No arrest was made.

At about 4:30 PM, officers on patrol in the 094XX block of S Lafayette Ave saw a subject in an alley bent over beside a parked car, holding a syringe and a small foil packet. The packet held a white powder that field-tested positive for heroin. The subject said they had found the packet and were only looking at it. Officers saw no one else in the area and found no cash or bags for packaging. The subject was taken into custody, and the items were inventoried.

At about 10:00 AM, the victim reported that a catering tray rack valued at about $150 had been left on the sidewalk beside their van on the street in the 031XX block of W Warren Blvd during a delivery. When they came back from the building, it had been taken. The van doors were closed and untouched. Nobody spoke to the victim, and there was no confrontation. The victim could not find anyone who had seen what happened. No arrest was made.

At about 10:13 PM, a clerk at a convenience store in the 006XX block of N Mc Clurg Ct reported that a customer picked up a bottle of wine, a sandwich, and a pack of energy drinks, then walked out without stopping at the register. The clerk shouted after them. The customer turned around, said "Put it on my tab," and continued walking. The clerk did not follow and no threats were made. The store's video will be reviewed. No arrest was made.

At about 9:21 PM, officers responded to a residence yard in the 002XX block of E 51st St, where the victim was bleeding from a cut on the shoulder. The victim stated that a neighbor came through the gate during an argument over a dog and swung a box cutter at them. Paramedics treated the victim. The neighbor, found nearby with the box cutter, said the victim had thrown the first punch, but no injury was seen on the neighbor. The box cutter was inventoried, and the neighbor was taken into custody.

At about 3:30 PM, a staff member on public school grounds in the 006XX block of N Lawndale Ave reported that one student shoved another into a fence after dismissal, and that the second student received a small scrape. Both had been arguing over a shared phone, which was not taken from either of them. The students were separated, and a parent came to pick up the injured student. The principal was informed. No weapons were involved, and no arrest was made.

At about 11:30 PM, the victim reported that their ex-wife came to their residence in the 070XX block of S Elizabeth St and banged on the door, despite a court order prohibiting any contact. She shouted through the door, then left when a porch light came on. She made no attempt to force the door and did not damage anything. Officers confirmed the order was valid and had been served. She was not at her listed address, and no arrest was made.

At about 9:32 PM, the victim reported at their residence in the 060XX block of S Rockwell St that their former partner had sent more than 60 text messages and social media posts that day calling them names and telling them they would regret leaving. No threat of specific violence was made, and the former partner did not come to the house. The victim saved screenshots for officers. There is no court order in place. No arrest was made.

At about 3:40 PM, the victim reported that their hatchback was gone from the street in the 028XX block of W Belmont Ave. The victim had lent it to no one and held the only key. City records showed no tow. A store camera showed two people working at the driver's door for under a minute before driving it away. The victim was not present, and no one was confronted. The plate was entered into the system. No arrest was made.

At about 12:51 AM, officers on patrol in the 079XX block of S Exchange Ave saw a man and a woman arguing beside a parked car. The woman stated that her boyfriend had grabbed her by the jacket and pushed her against the car when she tried to take the keys. Officers saw a red mark on her neck. The boyfriend said that the keys were his and denied touching her, but a passerby confirmed the push. She declined medical care. The boyfriend was taken into custody.

At about 11:00 AM, a homeowner in the 063XX block of S Artesian Ave reported that a riding mower valued at about $1,800 was gone from their unfenced side yard. The garage and house were closed and undamaged, and the mower had not been kept inside either one. Tire marks ran across the lawn toward the alley. The neighbors saw a trailer the previous afternoon but thought it was a landscaping crew. No arrest was made.

Officers responded to an apartment in the 032XX block of S Princeton Ave at about 9:50 AM. The victim stated that their adult son demanded money and, when refused, pushed them into a door frame. A bruise was forming on the victim's shoulder, and the victim declined treatment. No money was handed over or taken. The son was still in the apartment, admitted that he had shoved the victim, and said it was an accident. The son was taken into custody.

At about 7:30 PM, the victim reported that their car, parked on the street in the 078XX block of S Bennett Ave, had a smashed side mirror and paint poured on the hood. The victim had been visiting a relative for about an hour. All doors remained locked, and a wallet left in the console was still there. A child playing nearby said an adult had walked past the car, but no description was available. No arrest was made.

At about 7:18 PM, a security guard at a department store in the 076XX block of S Cicero Ave reported that a shopper took three pairs of shoes from a display, removed them from the boxes, and left through a side exit, setting off the alarm.
